description:
RFC 8620 §5.4 defines two arguments for the implicit Foo/set
destroy emitted by Foo/copy when onSuccessDestroyOriginal is true:

- onSuccessDestroyOriginal: Boolean (default false)
- destroyFromIfInState: String|null — passed as the ifInState
  argument to the implicit Foo/set call

Audit of the workspace shows none of the 7 *-server siblings honor
destroyFromIfInState; mail-server is the canonical template and
ignores it too:

  jmap-mail-server/src/email.rs:2282-2576   honors onSuccessDestroyOriginal
                                            but never reads destroyFromIfInState
  jmap-filenode-server/src/filenode.rs (post bd:JMAP-510h.56) honors
                                            onSuccessDestroyOriginal,
                                            does NOT read destroyFromIfInState
                                            (matched canonical mail-server
                                            coverage)
  jmap-chat-server, calendars-server, tasks-server, contacts-server,
  sharing-server: Foo/copy is either stubbed or not implemented;
  destroyFromIfInState gap is latent there too.

Failure mode: client A reads source records at state S12, then issues
Foo/copy with onSuccessDestroyOriginal:true and destroyFromIfInState:S12
to ensure the implicit destroy only proceeds if the source is unchanged.
Meanwhile client B mutates the source to S13. The handler ignores
destroyFromIfInState, the implicit destroy proceeds, and client A may
have destroyed data they did not intend to.

Per workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' rule, the fix lands first
on jmap-mail-server (the canonical extension-server template), then
propagates in the same pass to every extension-server sibling that
implements Foo/copy. Today that is mail-server and filenode-server;
when chat/calendars/tasks/contacts/sharing implement Foo/copy they must
include the check.

Required fix shape on canonical:
1. Parse destroyFromIfInState from args alongside onSuccessDestroyOriginal.
2. Before running the implicit destroys, compare the current source-
   account state to the destroyFromIfInState argument; if mismatched,
   produce a notDestroyed entry of type 'stateMismatch' per RFC 8620
   §5.3 SetError semantics for the implicit Foo/set call. (The
   implicit Foo/set response carries the standard newState/oldState
   wire shape, so the client sees the failure there.)
3. Mirror to filenode-server in the same commit.

Test discipline: add a regression test that proves the wire-format
notDestroyed entry surfaces 'stateMismatch' on the implicit Foo/set
response when destroyFromIfInState does not match the current source
state, and that the source data is left untouched.

Independent oracle: RFC 8620 §5.4 verbatim text in
~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec/references/rfc8620.txt:2255-2268.
title: destroyFromIfInState ignored in Foo/copy across all 7 extension-server siblings (workspace-canonical)
